If your dishwasher won’t turn on at all (no lights, no sounds, completely dead), it’s usually due to one of a few common issues. Here’s a step-by-step troubleshooting guide:

### 1. Check the Power Source
• Is it plugged in? Some dishwashers have a plug under the sink or inside the cabinet. Make sure it’s firmly connected.
• Tripped GFCI outlet: If your dishwasher is on a GFCI (Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter) outlet, check if the “Reset” button has popped out. Press it to reset.
• Tripped circuit breaker: Check your home’s electrical panel for any tripped breakers. Reset any that are in the middle or off position.

### 2. Check the Door Latch/Switch
Dishwashers won’t start if they don’t detect that the door is fully closed and latched.
• Close the door firmly and listen for a click.
• Inspect the latch mechanism for damage or obstruction.
• If the door switch is faulty, the dishwasher may not receive power to start. This often requires professional repair.

### 3. Check the Control Lock/Child Lock
Some models have a “Control Lock” or “Child Safety Lock” feature that disables all buttons.
• Look for a lock icon on the display or control panel.
• Refer to your manual to disable it (often involves holding a specific button for 3–5 seconds).

### 4. Reset the Dishwasher
Sometimes electronics glitch. Try resetting it:
• Turn off the power at the circuit breaker for 1–2 minutes, then turn it back on.
• Or unplug the dishwasher (if accessible) for a few minutes, then plug it back in.

### 5. Check for a Delayed Start
Some models have a “Delay Start” feature that can make it appear as though the unit is off. Check if a timer or delay indicator is lit on the display. Cancel any active delays.

### 6. Inspect the Control Panel/Touchpad
• If your dishwasher has a touch panel, moisture or cleaning products may have caused a short or stuck button. Try gently wiping it with a dry cloth.
• If buttons are unresponsive, the control board or touchpad may need replacement.

### 7. Check for Error Codes
If any lights flash or an error code appears (even if the display is otherwise dark), note it and consult your manual or search online for that specific code.

---

### When to Call a Professional:
• If you’ve checked power, reset the unit, and confirmed the door latch works—but still no response.
• If you smell burning or see signs of electrical damage.
• If you’re uncomfortable working with electrical components.

Its a Neff integrated one, 6 years old. No lights at all, nothing on display. Was fine yesterday. Consumer unit hasn't tripped and other sockets work.

Since the consumer unit (breaker) hasn’t tripped and other outlets are working, the issue is likely isolated to the dishwasher’s power supply or internal components. Here’s a focused troubleshooting plan for your 6-year-old Neff integrated dishwasher:

### 1. Check the Dedicated Circuit
• Even if the main consumer unit hasn’t tripped, some dishwashers have their own dedicated circuit breaker in the fuse box. Locate it and ensure it’s fully “on.”
• If unsure, turn the breaker off for 30 seconds, then back on to reset it.

### 2. Inspect the Plug/Connection
• Neff integrated dishwashers are often hardwired or plugged into a socket under the sink.
• If plug-in: Unplug and replug firmly. Check if the socket is live using another device (e.g., a lamp).
• If hardwired: Turn off power at the breaker, then check for loose wires in the junction box under the sink or behind the dishwasher.

### 3. Test the Door Latch/Switch
• A faulty door latch can prevent power from reaching the control panel.
• Close the door firmly and listen/feel for a click.
• If accessible, check the latch mechanism for damage or misalignment.

### 4. Reset the Control Panel
• Turn off power at the breaker for 1–2 minutes, then restore it. This can clear electronic glitches.

### 5. Check for Control Lock/Child Safety Mode
• Some Neff models have a control lock feature that disables all functions. Refer to your manual to disable it (often involves holding a specific button).

### 6. Inspect the Control Panel/Touchpad
• Moisture or cleaning residue can cause touchpad failures. Wipe the panel with a dry cloth.
• If unresponsive, the control board may need replacement.

### 7. Look for Error Codes
• Even if no lights are on, some Neff models blink LEDs in patterns to indicate faults. Check for any faint flashes behind the display or buttons.

### 8. Consider Internal Faults
• If all else fails, the issue may be internal:
• Power supply board: Failed to deliver voltage to controls.
• Control panel: Damaged or disconnected.
• Wiring: Loose connections inside the unit.

### Next Steps:
• If you’re comfortable with basic electrical checks (plug/socket, breaker), try those first.
• For internal repairs (latch, control board, wiring), contact Neff support or a qualified appliance technician. Mention the model number for accurate parts/service.
